text:
maya: Observed a sustained throughput drop on cluster-gpu-pool-7 starting ~12:10 UTC. p99 jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s and several workers restarted with OOMs. Attach initial traces and a quick summary below.

liam: Can you paste the worker logs?

maya: Paste from one restart (snip):
```
[2026-03-18T12:11:02Z] runtime: worker-23 PID=4121 gpu=0 OOM at alloc arena: slab_alloc failed, attempt=1 size=420M
[2026-03-18T12:11:02Z] runtime: kernel fallback: selected nv_fast_attn_v2 -> fallback nv_attn_generic due to memfrag
[2026-03-18T12:11:02Z] runtime: kvcache evict loop start: evicted=0MB try_bump=1
[2026-03-18T12:11:02Z] ccache: sweep slow path activated: sweep_time=1200ms (> target 200ms)
[2026-03-18T12:11:02Z] worker: restarting to recover slab state
```

sofia: incident-bot created incident #4532 (auto-detected throughput drop) :rotating_light:

oliver: nvidia-smi around that time?

maya: nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
Thu Mar 18 12:11:01 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. |
|  0   A100-SXM-80GB     On     | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   GI   CI       PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory |
|    0      0    0     4121     C   runtime_worker                     76336MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

liam: 76GB used — that’s near capacity for 80GB instance. But the logs show small-ish alloc (420M) triggered OOM; smells like fragmentation.

maya: Agreed. Also saw many short-lived KV cache evictions. p50 token-per-sec dropped 30% concurrently.

liam: Did kernel selection change? Any pattern in mode switch?

maya: From runtime debug stream: `kernel_hint(seq=128)=nv_fast_attn_v2` -> `alloc fail` -> fallback path uses `nv_attn_generic` which increases temporary memory by ~2-3x. That then triggers more evictions.

sofia: Sounds like a positive feedback loop: fallback kernel uses more ephemeral workspace, causes evict, which causes cache misses and higher memory footprint -> more fallbacks -> restarts.

oliver: Any recent kernel heuristics rollout? eng-runtime, did we push a heuristic change in the last deploy window?

liam: We rolled kernel heuristics 03/17 23:45 UTC with the ‘aggressive-fast-path’ tweak (PR #6082). It prefers nv_fast_attn_v2 for mid-length sequences. Possibly optimistic workspace estimate.

maya: Profiling capture shows workspace reservation mismatch: allocator reserved contiguous slab segments but slower GPU page-sweep meant freed pages weren't coalescing quickly (``sweep_time`` logged at 900-1200ms spikes). That allowed fragmentation to accumulate across requests.

oliver: Could noisy tenant be causing small allocations that fragment the big slab? Any tenant logs?

maya: Yes — tenant 'chatty-ai' had many tiny concurrent sessions sending short chats, causing repeated small allocations (~1-8MB) and freeing patterns. Combined with slow sweep, large contiguous views fail.

liam: Proposed mitigation options (short-term):
- revert aggressive-fast-path kernel heuristic to previous conservative thresholds (rollback PR #6082)
- enable compact-sweep mode on pool-7 to force coalescing more frequently (cost: CPU/GPU stall)
- increase ephemeral workspace cap to avoid fallback (temporary, increases chance of OOM)

sofia: Also worth adding temporary routing: divert chatty-ai traffic to dedicated smaller instances to reduce multi-tenant pressure. Ops can create a route rule for the customer.

oliver: I'm +1 to revert heuristics first (fast rollback) and flip compact-sweep for pool-7 as a second-stage if p99 doesn't recover. Can ops stand up routing rule now?

incident-bot: action: rollback job queued for PR #6082. ETA ~6m.

maya: After rollback triggered (12:18 UTC) we saw p99 drop to ~230ms within 4 minutes and worker restarts stopped. Throughput recovered to ~95% baseline.

liam: Good signal. We should still harden: add better workspace-aware kernel selection (account for fragmentation metrics), and emit kernel selection reason in traces.

sofia: Filed follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME-237 (kernel selection resilient to fragmentation), ENG-OPS-142 (pool-level auto-compact-sweep), ENG-INFR-88 (route noisy tenants by heuristic).

oliver: For the postmortem: include timeline, kernel heuristic diff, probe results (sweep_time histograms), and a small repro using interleaved tiny allocs + mid-length seqs to show the fallbacks.

maya: Adding reproduction note: run 128-seq workload with a high fanout of 1-8MB ephemeral allocations (script in gist) while toggling aggressive-fast-path. It reliably triggers OOMs on 80GB GPUs in ~5-10 minutes.

liam: Will add perf counters to kernel selection logs (workspace_est, free_contig_best, sweep_time) and a Canary that watches for OOMs after fallback to auto-disable heuristics on a pool.

sofia: Closing incident thread; incident-bot will generate ticket and slack summary. :white_check_mark:
